correctness.rationale: Every irreducible oversemigroup with Frobenius 14 through 27 is enumerated by the complete symmetric/pseudo-symmetric complement-pair choices and finite addition-closure tests. The smaller-F factors cannot cover special gaps. The proof of special-gap coverage for ordinary semigroups is elementary using multiples in the interval 14 through 27. The standalone verifier obtains 285 relevant factors and 163 distinct masks, excludes all three-factor covers, and enumerates every four-factor set. Its two independent finite combinatorial counting methods agree at 56, with 28 for each stated Frobenius signature; independent direct bit enumeration validates the irreducibility generator for all smaller F through 13. Computations and their finite, not infinite, scope are explicitly stated.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Existing construction of a decomposition of every length does not classify all distinct shortest decompositions. A general irreducible-factor enumeration algorithm is not an enumeration of the distinct shortest decompositions of H28.

originality.rationale: The 2026 motivating source is explicitly credited for the first exceptional multiplicity, its four-factor example, and the interval construction. The new, substantially stronger assertion classifies and counts every shortest decomposition and their complete Frobenius signatures. Close literature was inspected and targeted scholarly and mathematical record searches did not show equivalent/broader count tables. Search absence alone is not novelty proof and historical priority remains provisional.
residual_risks: Earlier unindexed or unpublished small-multiplicity tables may contain the same enumeration.
The seven-mask classification is a finite exhaustive result, not an extension to arbitrary multiplicities.

value.rationale: The natural first counterexample to the published constructive length threshold is the earliest distinguished benchmark for shortest decomposition phenomena. The exact 56-count, rigid two-profile Frobenius spectrum, and seven-by-three-binary-choice parametrization show the full shape and multiplicity of its optimal irreducible realizations; these are new structural data not determined by a single exceptional witness. Complete data for this precise boundary is useful for studying and testing future length-set classifications. The result deliberately makes no claim of larger downstream theorem.
